data.title: Tazarotene 0.1% (gel, cream)
data.summary: VII Anti-acne — Retinoids · Third-generation acetylenic retinoid (prodrug of tazarotenic acid)
data.body:
_Topicals · VII Anti-acne — Retinoids_

**Class:** Third-generation acetylenic retinoid (prodrug of tazarotenic acid)

## Mechanism of action
- Tazarotenic acid binds RAR-β and RAR-γ
- Normalises keratinocyte differentiation and proliferation, reduces inflammatory markers (psoriasis); induces tazarotene-induced genes (TIG1–3)
- Comedolytic in acne

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Plaque psoriasis (0.05%/0.1%) — often with a topical steroid to reduce irritation
- Acne vulgaris (0.1%; foam 0.1%; 0.045% lotion)
- Photoageing, nail psoriasis (off-label), congenital ichthyoses, keratosis pilaris

## Dose & formulations
- Thin layer once daily in the evening to lesions only (avoid surrounding skin in psoriasis)
- Short-contact therapy (wash off after 2–5 min, increasing) reduces irritation

## Adverse effects
- Irritation (most irritating topical retinoid): burning, redness, peeling
- Photosensitivity

## Contraindications
- Pregnancy (contraindicated — old FDA category X); women must have a negative pregnancy test and use contraception
- Eczematous or sunburnt skin

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated in pregnancy (old FDA category X).

## Viva points
- Only topical retinoid that is pregnancy category X
- Used for both psoriasis and acne
- Most irritating — combine with a steroid or use short contact

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.46; Khopkar ch.24. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
